slides.title: ماں بولی کدے نہ مُکے
slides.sub: صدیاں پرانے بول، اج وی ساڈے
slides.en: Verses centuries old, still ours. Four poets of Punjab, in their own words.

slides.gist: Calling out “Ranjha, Ranjha”, I have become Ranjha myself. Call me Dhido Ranjha now; let no one call me Heer.
Farid, do not scorn the dust; nothing is as great as dust. While we live it lies beneath our feet; when we die, it lies over us.
Hearts are deeper than rivers and seas; who can know what a heart holds? Inside it are the boats, the storms, the oars and the boatmen.
Roses do not keep their bloom forever, nor gardens their spring; nor will the parrots and bees keep circling forever.
slides.close: ایہناں بولاں نوں اسیں سانبھ رہے آں

carousels.caption_top:
ماں بولی کدے نہ مُکے 🤍
May our mother tongue never fall silent.

Four verses that Punjab has carried for centuries: Bulleh Shah, Baba Farid, Sultan Bahu and Mian Muhammad Bakhsh.
carousels.caption_end:
These words were sung in our grandparents' courtyards. If we don't read them, who will?
We are building a home for Punjabi poetry in Shahmukhi, with the meaning of every word. Coming soon.

slides.title: فریدا
slides.sub: اٹھ سو ورھے پرانے بول، اج وی سچے
slides.en: Baba Farid wrote these lines eight centuries ago. They still hold.

slides.gist: My bread is of wood; hunger is my relish. Those who eat buttered bread will suffer much pain.
Farid, the nights are long; my sides ache and ache. Cursed is the life of those who set their hope on others.
My body burns like an oven, my bones like firewood. I would walk till my feet tire, then on my head, if I might meet my Beloved.
Farid, make your mind a level field; smooth its pits and mounds. Then the fire of hell will never come near you.
slides.close: ایہناں بولاں نوں اسیں سانبھ رہے آں

carousels.caption_top:
فریدا 🤍
Four shaloks of Baba Farid, the first great poet of Punjabi, written some eight hundred years ago.
carousels.caption_end:
Punjabi poetry did not begin yesterday. Read it, say it aloud, pass it on.

Save this for a quiet night.

slides.title: رب کتھے لبھدا اے؟
slides.en: Where is God found? Three Sufi poets of Punjab answer.

slides.gist: If God were found by bathing and washing, the frogs and fish would find Him. God is found, Bahu, by those whose intentions are pure.
O Lord, You alone know my state. You are within, You are without, You are in every pore. Says humble Hussain: I am nothing, all is You.
Read the one Alif and be free. From one Alif came two, three, four, then thousands beyond counting; the point of that one Alif stands apart.
This body is the chamber of the true Lord; look within, O faqir. Do not beg favours of Khwaja Khizr: the water of life is inside you.
slides.close: ایہناں بولاں نوں اسیں سانبھ رہے آں

carousels.caption_top:
رب کتھے لبھدا اے؟ 🤍
Where is God found? Sultan Bahu, Shah Hussain and Bulleh Shah all point the same way: inward.
carousels.caption_end:
Our grandparents knew these lines by heart. Let's not be the generation that forgets them.
